Load 26: the view origin, column $7F and row $06 in characters. The screen builder $6D17 halves them at $6D26 and $6D2B to find the first metatile to draw; $6D8B–$6DA0 copies them to the left and top view bounds and computes right and bottom by adding $25 and $12 modulo 256; $6DA3–$6DBE scrolls once more down or right for an odd row or column; and $6DC1–$6DD6 stores the final bounds, adding $26 and $13. $33EC–$3408 saves both bytes, puts the current view's left and top ($569B, $569D) there for $6D17 to redraw the screen, and restores them.
The little-endian address $AC61 of this load’s entity records. $1863 copies it into the pointer at $E2–$E3.

The initial entity-slot limit is 4. $186D copies it to $4DBA, which bounds the slots that entity records fill: the initializer at $1863 loads records into slots 1 to 4 ($18CB). The load has 8 entity records, so the initializer stops at the limit with records 5–8 left; each pass, the slot scan at $3622 checks slots 1 to 4 ($3629), and $3632 gives an empty slot the next record (counter $7C) or, once the zero byte after record 8 is reached, reloads the slot's own record at $366A.

A 256-byte lookup indexed by screen character value: entry N is the colour-RAM byte for character N. After $6D17 draws the 20-by-10 metatile map window, it jumps to $6F3E, whose loop at $6F59–$6F5F reads each character of that screen buffer and writes the corresponding table byte to colour RAM, 39 columns by 20 rows from $D8C8. The view-shift routines read the table the same way for the column or row a scroll exposes: $30E1 for the right column, $319C for the left column, $3256 for the bottom row and $3314 for the top row. The visual-selector screens take their colours from the tables at $7F9E/$7FA5 instead, through $70ED. The table continues across $8000.
Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte attribute table indexed by the map's metatile value. The player's downward check tests bits 0–1 at $0C57 and, for the next column, at $0C7A; the player's horizontal checks at $0EB8 and $1051 test bit 1 when clipping the player against a tile. For entities, the downward scan at $450C tests bits 0–1 at $4532 and $4542, and the horizontal test at $460C reads four attributes through $4632 (at $464C), keeping bit 1 of the first two and bit 0 of the last two.

A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of top-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D53 writes the selected code to the cell to the right of the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and ($5A) at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of bottom-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D5A writes the selected code to one 40-character screen row below the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and ($58) at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

A 256-byte table of bottom-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D60 writes the selected code to one row below and one cell to the right of the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

The view starts one column past the declared width: $7F4D is 127, so when the load starts the full-screen draw at $6D41 reads columns 63–82 of rows 4–13, and the right edge $569C starts at 165, the right half of column 82; a vertical scroll that reaches this row while the view is there reads the same columns through $2E77 or $2F45. The player's right-hand wall test at $0EA1–$0EB5 reads two columns past the player's column $6F3C, so at the start view it reaches columns 82 and 83.

Use selected-player index $4DBD. If $4DC7,Y is nonzero, or if $4DC9,Y is at least stage field $4789,X under an unsigned byte comparison, go to $9A7F. Otherwise inspect stage field $4753,X. Reached when stage field $4753,X is 3 or has bit 0 clear: select message $9EC9 and jump to the message call at $9D1B. Load 26 never runs this path: it is reached only through the entry at $9A2B, which no stage record or instruction in the load or the resident part names.

Reached when stage field $4753,X is not 3: test its bit 0. A clear bit selects message $9EC9; a set bit calls $9D62, which stores $FF in $4753,X, then selects message $9EB3 and jumps to the message call at $9D1B. Load 26 never runs this path: it is reached only through the entry at $9A2B, which no stage record or instruction in the load or the resident part names.

Reached from the balance check when the gold covers stage field $4789,X. Test bit 0 of stage field $4753,X: clear selects message $9E75, set selects $9E5E. Both jump to $9C0E, which shows the message and starts the choice loop. Load 26 never runs this path: it is reached only through the entry at $9A2B, which no stage record or instruction in the load or the resident part names.

Load 26: the sufficient-gold message for a record whose $4753,X has bit 0 set, which the BNE at $9A84 takes: load message pointer $9E5E in X/Y and jump to $9C0E, which shows it and starts the choice. The eight-page character copy for visual selector 2, which starts at $9585, also takes $9A8D–$9A93 to $D508–$D50E as character $A1.

Save X in the immediate operand at $9ABC and Y in the one at $9AB7, call $36E9 to split A into nibbles plus one, clear the first two bytes at $9DD5, and write the tens and units codes to the next two bytes. A tens code of 1 is written as zero. Restore Y, call $9D7C, restore X and return. Its only callers, at $9A46 and $9A4E, are in the price setup, which load 26 does not run.

Load 26: the end of the price formatter $9A94: store the tens code, or 0 for a blank, at $9DD7, copy the units code $370A to $9DD8, then the LDY at $9AB6, whose operand $9AB7 holds the caller's Y saved by $9A97, the JSR $9D7C that draws the four digits with it, and the LDX at $9ABB, whose operand $9ABC holds the caller's X saved by $9A94; the RTS at $9ABD follows. The eight-page character copy for visual selector 2, which starts at $9585, also takes $9AAD–$9ABC to $D528–$D537 as characters $A5–$A6.

The flags come from the selection byte $9DDB, loaded at $9CA7 before the only jump here ($9CAA, taken when the layout gate $9DDA is nonzero): negative ($FF, left) enters the first-price balance check at $9AF0; zero selects message $9E9C at $9B3E; otherwise (1, right) take the second-price path at $9AC2. In load 26 the gate is nonzero only after the price setup at $9A37, which does not run, so this path does not run either.

Reached from $9ABE when the shop selection byte is 1. Load X from $7B and call $78D1 with stage field $4789,X, record byte 9, the second price: $78D1 subtracts it in packed decimal from the selected player’s gold and restores the gold if that borrows. Reload X and read callback high byte $4771,X. If nonzero, patch the JSR operand at $9AE0 from $476B/$4771 (record bytes 4 and 5), clear the high byte in the stage record so that the callback runs only once, and call the patched target; then use A=4 at $9B33, which adds it to the life meter. If zero, enter the message path at $9AE7, which shows message $9F0A and then does the same with A=4. No stage record in load 26 names this shop’s entry $9A2B (JMP $9A31), so this code does not run in load 26.

Second-price fallback: load X/Y with message $9F0A (“Nice and cold, / is'nt it?”, control byte $10, so the panel shows it for 16 updates), set A=4 and jump to $9B2E, which calls $77E0, pulls A and adds 4 to the selected player's life meter through $77A9. $9ACF branches here when the callback high byte $4771,X (record byte 5) is zero, after $78D1 has taken the second price, record byte 9, from the gold; the high byte is cleared once that record's callback has run. Load 26 never runs it: the purchase gate takes the price paths only when the layout gate $9DDA is nonzero, and no stage-object record in load 26 names the price set-up $9A2B; its records 1 and 2 name only the item-pair set-up $9A2E, which stores zero in the gate.

If selected-player high balance $4DC7,Y is zero and low balance $4DC9,Y is less than stage field $4783,X under an unsigned byte comparison, jump to $9C2E. Otherwise continue to the first-price payment at $9B05.

Load 26: the start of the first-price purchase, which the BNE at $9AF8 and the BCS at $9B00 take when the selected player's gold covers the first price: take the first price $4783,X from the gold through $78D1 and reload X from $7B. $9B0D then reads the record's first-item callback high byte $477D,X and goes to the fallback at $9B28 when it is zero. The eight-page character copy for visual selector 2, which starts at $9585, also takes $9B05–$9B0C to $D580–$D587 as character $B0.

First-price fallback: load X/Y with message $9F25 (“How do you like / the cocktail?”, control byte $10, so the panel shows it for 16 updates), set A=8 and fall into $9B2E, which calls $77E0, pulls A and adds 8 to the selected player's life meter through $77A9. $9B10 branches here when the callback high byte $477D,X (record byte 7) is zero, after $78D1 has taken the first price, record byte 8, from the gold; the high byte is cleared once that record's callback has run. Load 26 never runs it: the purchase gate takes the price paths only when the layout gate $9DDA is nonzero, and no stage-object record in load 26 names the price set-up $9A2B; its records 1 and 2 name only the item-pair set-up $9A2E, which stores zero in the gate.

Push A, call $77E0 with the message pointer in X/Y and pull A, then continue at $9B33, which adds A to the player’s meter through $77A9. The second-price fallback jumps here from $9AED with A=4 and message $9F0A; the first-price fallback falls in from $9B28 with A=8 and message $9F25. Load 26 never runs it: the purchase gate jumps to $9ABE only when the layout gate $9DDA is nonzero, and in load 26 only the item-pair setup, which stores zero there, runs.

Call $77A9 with A=4 or A=8, reload stage index, decrement $4753,X and jump to $9D1E. The two price paths jump here, $9AE4 with A=4 and $9B25 with A=8, after paying. $77A9 adds A to the selected player’s life meter $4DCD,Y, capped at the limit $4DCF,Y; $9D1E calls $3C2A and $370B until the message countdown $4D6B is zero and returns. No stage record in load 26 names this shop’s entry, so the code does not run in load 26.

Load X/Y with message pointer $9E9C and jump to the message call at $9D1B. $9AC0 branches here when the selection byte read at $9CA7 is zero. Load 26 never runs it: the purchase gate jumps to $9ABE only when the layout gate $9DDA is nonzero, and in load 26 only the item-pair setup, which stores zero there, runs.

Load 26: reload X from $7B, decrement the record's $4753,X, load message pointer $9EE6 in X/Y and jump to the message call at $9D1B. The only jump here is the JMP at $9C53 in the timeout path $9C4E, taken when the layout gate $9DDA is nonzero. The eight-page character copy for visual selector 2, which starts at $9585, also takes $9B45–$9B50 to $D5C0–$D5CB as characters $B8–$B9.

Store zero at the layout gate $9DDA, set sound state $2C15 to 2, and set $4D69 to 7. Reload stage index from $7B and continue to the item-pair selection at $9B62. The jump entry at $9A2E leads here. Both of load 26’s stage records, at $9029 and $9039, name that entry.

Store $46 plus one modulo 256 at $9D90. Pass the first selected item at $9DE0 to $9D97, then call $9D7C with Y=$73. Repeat for the second item at $9DE1 with Y=$87.

Call $3C2A, decrement $9DDF and branch to $9C4E at zero. Otherwise call $370B, $9D52 and $3C4C, then fall through to the sampled-input choice at $9C3F.

Use the sampled active-low inputs: if $70 is zero, branch to the shop gate at $9CA2; otherwise, if $73 is zero, branch to the left handler at $9C64; otherwise, if $74 is zero, branch to the right handler at $9C82. Reached when the countdown at $9DDF reaches zero. If $9DDA is nonzero, jump to $9B45. Otherwise load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X, load X/Y with message pointer $9E1C, and jump to the $77E0 call at $9D1B.

Read the layout gate $9DDA; if nonzero, load the selection byte $9DDB and jump to $9ABE. Otherwise load X from $7B and read $9DDB. Choose an item index using the incoming negative flag: load $9DE0 when it is set, or $9DE1 when clear, then enter the price selector at $9CD6. The path at $9CA2 supplies that flag from $9DDB.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts, use the result as Y, and copy the item row's price at $A131,Y and $A132,Y (row offsets 0 and 1) to $7D/$7E. Call $7901, which subtracts the packed-decimal amount from the selected player’s gold, restores it on insufficient funds, returns carry set on success and clears decimal mode. Load 26's shop records give items 6–18 here, all rows of the 24-row item table at $A131.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's purchase-routine address at $A135,Y and $A136,Y (row offsets 4 and 5) into the operand of the JSR at $9D14, which calls it with the item number plus 1 in A. Load 26's shop records give items 6–18 here, all rows of the 24-row item table at $A131.

Pull the selected item index, clear carry, add 1 in binary mode and call the JSR whose operand was patched by the selector. Load X/Y with $9E09 and call $77E0, then call $3C2A and $370B repeatedly while $4D6B is nonzero. Return once it is zero.
Load 26: return A unchanged unless it equals $13. For $13, inspect bit $10 of the selected player’s flags: return $14 when set, or $13 when clear. The shop item-pair path uses this resolver.
Test bit $10 of the flags in A. If clear, return A=$13; if set, return A=$14. This is the tail of the selected-item resolver, after the player flags have been loaded.

Load 26: call the input sampler at $3C4C and return carry set if any of $73, $74 or $70 is zero, that is while the stick is pushed left or right or fire is pressed (joystick port 2, active low); return carry clear if all are nonzero.

Load 26: with decimal mode clear, add one to the selection byte at $9DDB, use the wrapped result as an index into $9DDC, and pass that position in X and $82 in Y to $719E. The selection byte stays among $FF, 0 and 1, so the index is 0 to 2.
Load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X and return. The insufficient-gold path calls it at $9A75, and the item effects at $A1F1, $A1F7, $A1FD, $A203, $A209, $A212 and $A21E tail-call it.

Multiply A, an item's number, by 8 using three eight-bit shifts, clear carry, add 6 and use the eight-bit result as X. Read the high byte from $A132,X into Y and the low byte from $A131,X into X, the message pointer at offsets 6 and 7 of the item's row in the 24-row item table at $A131, then jump to $77E0. Entry $77E0 loads A=0, so the message routine uses X/Y as a direct pointer. The selection paths call this routine at $9C79 with the first item's number from $9DE0 and at $9C99 with the second's from $9DE1. Load 26's shop records give items 6–18 here, all rows of the table: record 1 at $9029 gives the selected player's $4DD7 byte (0–4) plus 13 and that plus one; record 2 at $9039 gives the selected player's $4DD9 byte (0–5) plus 6 and that plus one.

Load 26: process four price-display bytes at $9DD5 in reverse order. Leave zero unchanged; add $F5 to each nonzero byte with eight-bit wrap and decimal mode clear. Call the digit writer at $9D8E with successive Y positions, decrementing Y after each call.

Load 26: store A at offset Y of the page after $46, through STA $FF00,Y. $9A34 and $9BF1 each set its high byte $9D90 to $46 plus one, $C1 or $C5, since $46 holds the screen page $C0 or $C4; the load holds $FF there. Then write colour 1 to $D900,Y, the matching colour RAM, and return. Called from $9D86. Colour RAM requires I/O visible.

Load 26: multiply item ID A by eight with eight-bit wrap, split the two packed bytes from the item table at $A131 into four nibble-plus-one values at $9DD5, and replace consecutive leading ones with zero. Nibbles and item indexes are not locally validated.

Load 26: four working price-display bytes. The item-price formatter at $9D97 and the stage-price formatter at $9A94 write them, and the drawing loop at $9D7C reads them in reverse, from $9DD8 down to $9DD5, passing each to the digit writer at $9D8E.
